meta.name: CafeMenu
meta.title: CafeMenu · QR table ordering for small cafes
meta.description: Customers scan the code on their table and order from their phone. Staff see orders arrive live. Your menu, orders and data stay in your own free Firebase project.

status.label: Status
status.text: **Early development.** Sign-up isn't open yet. This page describes CafeMenu 1.0; follow the work [on GitHub](https://github.com/shreyashp47/cafemenu/milestones).

hero.title: QR table ordering for your cafe, on your own Firebase.
hero.lead: Customers scan the code on their table and order from their phone. Your staff see each order arrive live. You run the menu and read the numbers, and the menu, orders and data stay in **your** Google account.
hero.note: Built from TOE, which already takes real orders at a working cafe.
hero.shotCustomer: A customer's phone: the menu, with categories, prices, an item in the cart and one sold out
hero.shotStaff: The staff phone: the live order board with a table's order being prepared

points.title: No app to install
points.text: Customers scan and order in the browser. No login, no download.

points.title: Your data, your account
points.text: Everything lives in a Firebase project you own, not ours.

points.title: Free for a small cafe
points.text: Runs on Firebase's no-cost Spark plan. No card needed.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: Set up in a few minutes, guided at every step. You need a Google account, and nothing else to buy or install.

steps.title: Fill in a short form
steps.text: Cafe name, web address, country, number of tables, theme, logo and a starting menu.

steps.title: Create a free Firebase project
steps.text: In your own Google account, following step-by-step screenshots. The free Spark plan is enough.

steps.title: Give CafeMenu access
steps.text: Add CafeMenu as a member of that project, so it can set it up and send you updates. You can remove it at any time.

steps.title: Wait about a minute
steps.text: CafeMenu sets up the database, sign-in, your menu and your site, and shows each step as it goes. Then you choose your password from the email you receive.

steps.title: Print your table QR cards
steps.text: One card per table, straight from your dashboard. Put them out and take orders.

how.ownership: Your menu, orders and staff accounts live in **your** Firebase project, not ours. You choose when to take new releases, and you can leave at any time: your site keeps running on its last release.

cost.need: **You need:** a Google account. **Optional:** your own domain name, bought from any domain registrar, if you'd rather not use `your-cafe.web.app`.
cost.later: If paid plans ever come, they'll be announced well ahead, and your site keeps running in your own project whatever you decide.

try.title: Try it
try.lead: Sign-up isn't open yet, but the cafe app already runs on your own computer in demo mode, with a sample menu and no Firebase account. Customer and staff side by side, live.
try.needs: You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 20.9 or newer and git.
try.commands:
git clone https://github.com/shreyashp47/cafemenu.git
cd cafemenu
npm ci
npm run dev
try.then: Then open these two pages side by side and place an order:
try.local: Demo orders stay in your browser. Nothing is sent anywhere.
try.hosted: A hosted demo you can open from this page is on the way.
try.careful: **Please don't test on a real cafe's site.** Its order board is a real counter, and a test order there is a real order.

items.a: You do. Your menu, orders and staff accounts are stored in a Firebase project in your own Google account. CafeMenu keeps only what it needs to run your site: your email, your project's ID and web address, your cafe's settings, which release it runs, and a history of its deployments.

You add CafeMenu's service account as a member of your Firebase project. With that it sets the project up, deploys your site and its security rules, and moves your data forward when a release needs it. That access includes your order data, which is why it is spelt out here, in the privacy policy, and on the setup page, with a link to see or remove it.

CafeMenu ships numbered releases. By default your cafe follows **stable** and updates on its own; **beta** gets new versions first; or you can **stay on a version** and press Upgrade when you're ready. Security fixes still reach every cafe. If a release doesn't suit you, **Roll back** returns to the one before.
Remove CafeMenu's member from your project. Your site keeps running on its last release, and your data was always yours: nothing to export, nothing to ask for.

items.q: Do customers need an app or an account?
items.a: No. They scan the code on their table, order in the browser, and pay at the counter. No download, no login.

items.q: Which countries does it work in?
items.a: Any. Each cafe sets its own currency, time zone and date formats. The app is in English first, with every word in a translation file so more languages can follow.
Yes. CafeMenu is open source under the MIT licence, on [GitHub](https://github.com/shreyashp47/cafemenu), with the whole plan in the open.

project.title: Create a Firebase project
project.lead: Your cafe's site, menu and orders live in a Firebase project in **your own** Google account, not ours. It's free on the Spark plan, with no card needed.
steps: Open the [Firebase console](https://console.firebase.google.com/) and sign in with the Google account the cafe should belong to.
Press **Create a project** (some accounts say **Add project**). Name it after your cafe, like **{name}**.
Google Analytics isn't needed: you can turn it off.
Stay on the free **Spark** plan. CafeMenu never needs you to upgrade or add a card.
Wait for **Your new project is ready**, and press **Continue**.

access.title: Access
access.lead: CafeMenu sets your project up and keeps it updated through one member you added to it: its deploy account, which is a robot account rather than a person. What it can do is below, with how to check it and how to remove it.

account.label: The deploy account
account.none: Its address isn't set up on this site yet. CafeMenu's maintainer will send it to you.

access.roles: Its role in your project is [[SPIKE #3: the exact IAM roles, settled by the Phase 0 spike]].

can.title: What that allows
can.text: Close to admin. It can set up and change almost everything your cafe needs, and it **can technically read your orders**. It can't see your Google account, your other projects or your billing details, and it can't delete your project. [[SPIKE #3: confirm these limits once the roles are known]]

will.title: What CafeMenu will do
items: Set your cafe up, then deploy the releases you choose.
Deploy **security fixes** to every cafe, even one that chose to stay on an older version.
Run data migrations, using code that's public on GitHub.
Check each deploy works, and roll it back if it doesn't.
Look at a problem in your project **when you ask**, and only at what that problem needs.

wont.title: What it won't do
items: Read your orders, staff list or customers' data for its own purposes.
Sell, share or analyse your data, or use it for advertising.
Change your menu, prices or tables unless you ask (apart from loading your starting menu once, at setup).
Touch your billing or your other Google projects.

check.title: How to check it
check.lead: The Firebase console doesn't list robot accounts among a project's members, so you won't see CafeMenu there, even when it's connected. Use the Google Cloud IAM page:
steps: Open the [Google Cloud IAM page]({url}), signed in with the Google account that owns your cafe's project.
Make sure your cafe's project is picked at the top of the page.
On the **View by principals** tab, find the deploy account. The **Role** column shows what it has.
check.more: If it has any role that isn't listed above, tell CafeMenu's maintainer: it shouldn't. What it has done in your project is in **Logging** → **Logs Explorer** on the same console.

remove.title: How to remove it
steps: On the same IAM page, tick the box next to the deploy account.

leaving.title: What happens if you leave
leaving.lead: From the moment you remove it:
items: CafeMenu can't reach your project at all.
Updates **and security fixes** stop.
Your site keeps running on its last release, and your data stays in your project, where it always was.
leaving.back: Changed your mind? Add the member again, and ask CafeMenu's maintainer to check the connection.
leaving.delete: To delete your CafeMenu account as well, see [Leaving](https://github.com/shreyashp47/cafemenu/blob/main/docs/legal/privacy-policy.md#7-leaving-and-deleting-your-console-data).

search.label: Find an owner or cafe
search.hint: By email, owner's or cafe's name, web address or Firebase project ID.

directory.ownersError: The owners directory couldn't be read: emails and names come from the cafes only.
directory.ownersLag: The owners directory is copied from Authentication every hour, so a new account can take that long to appear.

cafe.back: Back to every owner and cafe
cafe.notFound: That cafe is no longer in the list: it may have been deleted.

actions.title: Actions
actions.cannot: Actions go through the backend on GitHub Actions, which this console isn't set up to use: set `NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND=requests` (see the README). Until then this page only reads.

explain.suspend: The owner can't sign in to the console, their requests are refused with the reason, rollouts skip their cafes, and they're emailed. Their site keeps running as it is. Reactivating undoes all of it.
explain.reactivate: Undoes the suspension: the owner can sign in again, their requests and updates go through, and they're emailed. A suspension still waiting for its date is called off.
explain.delete-owner: Deletes the owner's CafeMenu login and their records here: cafes, deployments and requests. The admin log keeps its entries. Nothing in their own Firebase project is touched, and their site keeps running without CafeMenu. This can't be undone.
explain.maintenance-on: Customers see a “back soon” page and can't order; orders already placed, the staff board and the owner's dashboard keep working. The owner is emailed with the reason, and only you can end it.
explain.maintenance-off: Ordering opens again, and the owner is emailed.

actions.noteHint: Goes in the owner's email and the admin log. Up to 500 characters.
actions.effectiveHint: The cafe's time ({zone}). Leave empty for now.
actions.notice: {reason} needs {days} days' notice: not before {when}. The owner is told now.
actions.deleteReminder: Before deleting: remove CafeMenu's deploy account from the project **{project}**, or ask the owner to (their Access page shows how), so CafeMenu keeps no access to it.
actions.deleteNoProject: This cafe never connected a project, so there's no access to remove.
actions.confirm: Type the cafe's web address to confirm
actions.messageHint: Optional, up to 280 characters. Without one they read “We're making a few changes”.
actions.untilHint: Optional: shown to customers. The cafe's time ({zone}).
actions.startsAtHint: Leave empty to start at the backend's next run. The cafe's time ({zone}).
actions.endsAtHint: Leave empty to end it yourself. The cafe's time ({zone}).
actions.asked: Asked. The backend's next run does it, within about 5 minutes; the history below shows how it went.
actions.noSite: This cafe has no site yet, so there's nothing to put into maintenance.
actions.adminOwner: This owner is an admin: remove them as admin before suspending or deleting them.

problems.notice: This reason needs notice: pick a time on or after {when}.
problems.bad-time: That isn't a date and time.
problems.confirm: That isn't this cafe's web address.
problems.ends-first: The end has to come after the start.
problems.email: That doesn't look like an email address.

bulk.title: Maintenance on several cafes
bulk.explain: One request per cafe, all in one batch. The times are read on each cafe's own clock. If this page closes partway, Resume picks up where it stopped; Revert turns maintenance off again on every cafe the batch turned it on.
bulk.untilHint: Optional: shown to customers. Read on each cafe's own clock.
bulk.startsAtHint: Leave empty to start at the backend's next run. Read on each cafe's own clock.
bulk.endsAtHint: Leave empty to end it yourself. Read on each cafe's own clock.

log.title: Admin log
log.explain: Every admin action, as the backend did it. Entries are written once and never changed, by anyone, the admin included.

search.label: Find in the log
search.hint: A cafe, an email, a reason or a note.

admins.title: Admins
admins.explain: Accounts with the admin flag, from the owners directory. The first is set once with `npm run make-admin` (see the platform functions README).
admins.none: No admin in the directory yet: it's copied from Authentication every hour.
admins.last: The only admin can't be removed.

appoint.title: Appoint an admin
appoint.off: Appointing more admins is off for now: section 8 of the requirements keeps it to the first admin. It's built in; turning it on is one setting (APPOINT_OTHER_ADMINS in @cafemenu/shared/admin-policy) and the backend's own check.

problems.site-format: Use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, up to 30 characters, not starting or ending with a hyphen.
problems.region-unknown: Choose where your database lives from the list.
problems.project-id-format: That doesn't look like a Firebase project ID. Copy it from Project settings in the Firebase console.
problems.settings-invalid: Some settings aren't valid. Check the fields marked.
problems.plan-locked: A new cafe starts on the free plan.
problems.pinned-format: Choose a version line such as 1.4.
problems.logo-not-png: That logo couldn't be read. Try a PNG, JPEG or WebP file.
problems.logo-too-big: That logo is too detailed to store. Try a simpler image or a smaller file.
problems.menu-template: Choose one of the starter menus.
problems.menu-currency: The menu's prices are in another currency. Check them again.
problems.menu-empty: A starter or a pasted list needs at least one item; a blank menu has none.
problems.menu-too-long: That's more than 200 items. Start with fewer and add the rest in your dashboard.
problems.menu-item: Some menu rows aren't complete. Check the rows marked.

errors.auth/invalid-email: That email address doesn't look right.
errors.auth/email-already-in-use: There is already an account with that email. Sign in instead.
errors.auth/weak-password: Use a password of at least 6 characters.
errors.auth/invalid-credential: That email and password don't match.
errors.auth/too-many-requests: Too many tries. Wait a minute and try again.
errors.auth/user-disabled: This CafeMenu account is suspended. CafeMenu has emailed you why; reply to that email to talk about it.
errors.auth/network-request-failed: No connection. Check the internet and try again.
errors.permission-denied: You can't do that here. If you just verified your email, reload the page.
errors.admin-pending: The backend doesn't take this yet. Nothing was changed.
errors.unimplemented: Checking isn't switched on yet. Your project ID is saved, and CafeMenu's maintainer will check the connection for you.
errors.failed-precondition: That can't be done right now: another update may be running, or the cafe isn't live. Try again in a minute.
errors.invalid-argument: That version can't be deployed to your cafe.
errors.backend-pending: Changes from here aren't switched on yet. Nothing was changed on your site.
errors.unavailable: CafeMenu couldn't reach Google just now. Try again in a minute.
errors.unexpected: Something unexpected went wrong. Try again in a few minutes.
errors.gave-up: CafeMenu tried several times and couldn't finish. Try again in a few minutes.
errors.cancelled: Called off before it was done.
